creep.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 5.13.3, Eq 6.5.3 and Figure 6.5.1 (pp. 856-857)
creep.note: Figure 6.5.1 digitised from the gazette at 5 % relative humidity steps (read to about ±0.05). The figure's curves start at about 30-40 % relative humidity: below 40 % the 40 % value is used. Between the printed ages of loading, thicknesses and humidities the coefficient is interpolated linearly (ages on a log scale); outside them the nearest printed value is used. The development between the printed shares (40 % at 1 month, 60 % at 6 months, 80 % at 30 months, all at 30 years) is interpolated on log(1 + days under load): SAEngine practice, not BNBC.

shrinkage.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 5.13.4, Eq 6.5.4 and Figure 6.5.2 (pp. 856-858)
shrinkage.note: Figure 6.5.2 digitised from the gazette at 5 % relative humidity steps (read to about ±5 × 10⁻⁶); negative values are swelling (above about 92 %). Shrinkage is proportional to the water content within 150-230 litre/m³ (190 litre/m³ for the figure). Eq 6.5.4 prints the divisor as 1 + kρ, with ρ the steel ratio and the coefficient K (25 internal, 15 external exposure) defined beside it: read as 1 + K ρ. Before 6 months the shrinkage is interpolated from zero at the start of drying on log(1 + days of drying), and between 6 months and 30 years on the same scale: SAEngine practice, not BNBC.

exposure.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Figures 6.5.1-6.5.2 (pp. 857-858): the indoor and outdoor exposure lines
exposure.note: The relative humidities are where the figures draw the indoor and outdoor exposure lines (about 45 % and 85 %). A project's own ambient humidity may replace them.

strengthGain.source: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: f'c(t) = t / (a + b t) × f'c (ACI 209R, moist-cured ordinary cement)
strengthGain.note: BNBC gives the modulus at 28 days only (Sec 5.13.2) and asks for the modulus at the age of loading Et in Eq 6.5.3, without a strength-age relation. SAEngine takes the strength gain t / (4 + 0.85 t), capped at f'c, and Et from the pack's Ec rule at that strength. Lower Et at early ages gives more creep: on the safe side for the shortening.

prestress.note: For the prestress losses (Part 8 prestressed design). Post-tensioned shrinkage is 0.0002 / log10(t + 2) with t the age at transfer in days.
